
=================================================================
#27 Nangbi  (629 flashback)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: Iron Will · tone: war-legend chronicle
Logline: Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
[1] [MAP 629: ]
[2] ¶ Autumn. Silla’s army is breaking against a Goguryeo wall. The men who should be charging are sitting in the trenches. Yushin is thirty-four, a banner captain. His white horse doesn’t even have a name.
[3] [battle]
[4] [PLACE nangbi: A Goguryeo wall that is about to make somebody famous.]
[5] ¶ He rides back to his father’s command post, gets down, and takes off his helmet, which is how a son asks permission in front of an army.
[6] Kim Yushin: Father. We’re losing. / They say you shake a coat by the collar to make it hang straight, and lift the head-rope to open a net. / …Let me be the collar.
[7] Kim Seohyun: …Put your helmet on. / Then go.
[8] ¶ The white horse takes the trench in one jump that the men in it will describe for the rest of their lives, usually with their hands. Mud to the girth. A horn somewhere, too late. The Goguryeo line bends where he hits it, like a wall that has just remembered it is made of men. In, out. In again. The third time Yushin comes back there is something heavy hanging from his saddle, and the men in the trench are already climbing out after him.
[9] [battle]
[10] ¶ He brings the weight on his saddle back to the command post and sets it down in the mud in front of his father, wrapped in a torn banner, because he does not know what else a son is supposed to do with a general’s head. The staff officers wait for the speech. Seohyun looks at the bundle, then at the boy, for long enough that someone coughs.
[11] Kim Seohyun: …Your helmet’s crooked.
[12] ¶ He reaches up and straightens it himself, both hands, the way you fix a boy’s collar before a feast, and then turns away and shouts for his officers before anyone can see his face. It is the most Kim Seohyun has ever said to his son about anything, and Yushin will carry it longer than the helmet.
[13] ¶ That night he asks the groom what the white horse is called. The groom says it has no name; it came from the royal stable as a spare. Yushin looks at it for a long time, at the mud on its chest and the way it still will not quite stand still.
[14] Kim Yushin: Hangyul. / …It means steady. It came back steady. All three times.
[15] ¶ The few who get out of Nangbi walk north for nine days with the story, and it grows a little at every well. By Pyongyang the white horse has cleared the trench at a gallop with a general’s head in one hand and a banner in the other, and the man on it has a name the Goguryeo clerks must write down for the first time.
[16] [battle]
[17] ── SCENE: The Pyongyang Court ──
[18] ¶ In Pyongyang the report is read to the king twice, the second time because he asks for it. At the back of the hall the Yeon heir, twenty-four, stands with his arms folded, the way he stands everywhere.
[19] King Youngryu: Kim Yushin… a banner captain. / We have never heard the name.
[20] Yeon Gesomun: You’ll hear it again. / One man jumps one ditch and five thousand of ours lie down. That’s a captain? That’s a sword. / Silla’s sword.
[21] ── SCENE: The High Commander’s House ──
[22] ¶ Gesomun’s family lives in the big house below the palace hill. His father, Yeon Taejo, has run the Summit for ten years. Long enough to outlive most of the men who voted for him. None of the ones who voted against. Most nights he comes home in a silence the servants have learned to walk around.
[23] ¶ Tonight he does not take off his boots. He sits at the low table with a copy of the Nangbi report, the one the king asked to hear twice, and reads it a third time with his finger under the lines.
[24] Yeon Gesomun: Father. You’re still on that? / It’s one fortress. We take it back by spring.
[25] Yeon Taejo: Sit. / …Five thousand heads. Off one charge. How many men have you seen do that?
[26] Yeon Gesomun: One. / You. At the Colossal River.
[27] Yeon Taejo: I had thirty thousand men, a river on my side, and Ulchi giving the orders. / He had a ditch and a horse.
[28] ¶ Gesomun has seen his father angry, drunk and bleeding, and once, when he was seven, riding home from the Colossal River with a Sui banner rolled under his arm like a bolt of cloth. He has never seen him frightened of a piece of paper. He finds he does not know where to put his hands.
[29] Yeon Taejo: Thirty-four, and still a banner captain. Silla won’t let a Gaya grandson climb any faster. / They’re wasting him. They won’t waste him forever.
[30] Yeon Gesomun: Then I’ll kill him before they stop.
[31] Yeon Taejo: You’ll try. / Listen to me. Never on a field he picked. Never when you’re angry. And when this city tells you he’s only a captain, don’t believe it.
[32] Yeon Gesomun: His Majesty already did.
[33] Yeon Taejo: His Majesty heard it twice and asked the Summit what to do. / Do you know what the Summit did? Argued half a day over who pays to rebuild the fort. Nobody said his name. Not once. / Ten years I’ve sat in that room. They’ll lose this country one granary at a time and call it caution.
[34] ¶ Each of them learns his country at home. Euija learns the great clans at his father’s table. Chunchu learns the council from the day it walked his grandfather off the throne. And Gesomun learns this city here, from an old man reading one report three times by lamplight. Nobody else in the city would read it once.
[35] Yeon Gesomun: …Kim Yushin.
[36] ¶ That’s where the name comes from. Not from his own capital, which likes its titles stamped and filed. From the people he beat. Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning. On the border, mothers use it to get children indoors before dark.
[37] ¶ Thirteen years later, Gesomun hears that sword is riding for the Silla envoy in his prison, and opens the cell. A few months after that, a laughing king says the name across a table. Gesomun’s cup stops an inch from his mouth. Now you know why.
[38] ¶ **Thirteen years on, the banner captain has a queen, a title, and forty fortresses Baekje just took from her. He wants them back…!**
